title: eMudhra intermediate CA certificates with recoverable P-384 private keys
summary: Eight intermediate CA private keys created in an eMudhra key ceremony on 2026-04-30 were generated with almost no entropy. Mozilla independently confirmed that every key was an integer below 256, i.e. recoverable by trying 256 candidates. A holder of a recovered key can mint certificates that an unpatched client accepts for any name (TLS) or for signed code (code signing). This is NOT evidence of malware on any machine: what an audit must answer is whether a client on this machine would still accept a chain through one of these keys.
primary_match_key_rationale: The same private key appears in both an eMudhra-signed certificate and a Sectigo 'AAA Certificate Services' cross-signed certificate, so the subject/issuer names and certificate fingerprints differ while the SubjectPublicKeyInfo is identical. Matching on SPKI SHA-256 therefore catches both signing paths with one indicator.
certificate_sha256_note: 16 impacted certificates exist (8 keys x 2 signing paths). Their individual SHA-256 fingerprints, serial numbers and PEM bodies are published by the upstream tracker but are deliberately NOT copied into this release; redistribution terms for that file have not been confirmed. SPKI matching already covers all 16, so no detection capability is lost. See docs/data-provenance.md.
certificate_count_derivation: 8 compromised keys x 2 signing paths (eMudhra-signed and Sectigo cross-signed) = 16 certificates

related_roots.note: Widely trusted Sectigo root used by many unrelated certificates. Its presence is expected and is never, on its own, an indicator.

root_presence_rationale: Clients can and do keep these roots trusted while rejecting the specific compromised SPKIs (Chrome blocked the SPKI hashes via CRLSet rather than removing a root). Reporting a trusted root as a risk would be a false positive.

network_test_hosts.purpose: serves a certificate chaining to a compromised intermediate so that a successful TLS handshake indicates the client still trusts it
network_test_hosts.privacy_note: Connecting discloses your source IP address, TLS fingerprint and User-Agent to a third party that publishes aggregate statistics. Never contacted unless --network-test is passed explicitly with a host.

timeline.event: Key generation ceremony that produced the eight weak keys.
Chrome blocked the affected SPKI hashes via CRLSet by 19:45 UTC.
eMudhra root-cause investigation still open; wrap/unwrap step on the HSM reported as the suspected origin.

credential_guidance.principle: A weak CA key creates the capability for interception; it does not by itself show that any password or token on a given machine was intercepted. An audit tool must neither order a blanket rotation nor declare rotation unnecessary. It reports a conditional scope and the escalation criteria.

conditions.when: A client on this machine accepted a compromised SPKI during some window, with no further evidence.
do: Identify which destinations were contacted during the window.
Review authentication logs, proxy logs and certificate logs for that window.
Do not rotate everything reflexively; scope by what the evidence covers.

conditions.when: Suspicious certificates, anomalous authentications, session misuse or tampered packages were observed.
do: Reset passwords for the accounts known to be affected.
Revoke the related sessions and authentication tokens.
Rotate API keys, deploy keys and CI secrets that could have been exposed.
Have users change reused passwords on other services.
This exceeds the scope of an endpoint audit: escalate to the organisation's incident response plan and follow the prescribed order of operations.

sources.used_for: evidence-scoped credential response: reset passwords for known affected users, monitor authentication logs, assess API keys tied to known affected identities, advise users to change reused passwords
broader systemic-compromise measures and the requirement to carry out steps in the prescribed order
independent confirmation of key recoverability; enumeration of 8 direct + 8 cross-signed certificates
impact description and Chrome CRLSet blocking timestamp
vendor statement, suspected cause, no known prior misuse
impact is certificate authentication, not the TLS ciphers; do not disable verification
SPKI SHA-256 values transcribed into compromised_intermediates

limitations: The root cause was still under investigation as of 2026-10-21.

eMudhra states no end-entity certificates were issued from these intermediates and reports no evidence of prior misuse; code-signing certificates are not covered by Certificate Transparency, so CT logs cannot establish absence of misuse for the code-signing keys.
Cloudflare observed no active exploitation on its own network, which is not evidence about other networks.
